chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a one-eyed man whose healthy eye was struck and blinded: 'He may blind one of the eyes of his companion, and half the blood-money is settled for him; and if he wishes, he may take a complete blood-money, and be excused from the eye of his companion.'
ai.seo_question: What are the legal options for retaliation when a one-eyed person blinds the healthy eye of another?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Baqir (AS), establishes the principle of 'equal for equal' in qisas (retaliation) while accommodating the unique physiological state of the victim. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the value of an eye in a one-eyed person is half that of a two-eyed person, allowing the victim to choose between proportional physical retaliation with reduced compensation or full blood-money (diya) with forgiveness. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic penal law to ensure justice is both precise and equitable.
